prompt:
A sealed rigid flask contains 0.20 mol of helium gas at an initial temperature of 27 degrees Celsius (300 K). Helium may be assumed to behave as an ideal gas. Take the molar gas constant R = 8.31 J K^-1 mol^-1.
(a) Calculate the total internal energy of the helium gas in the flask. [2]
(b) The gas is heated electrically so that 150 J of thermal energy is transferred to the gas. No gas escapes and the volume of the flask remains constant. Calculate the new temperature of the gas in kelvin. [2]

mark_scheme.criterion: (a) Uses U = (3/2) nRT with n = 0.20 mol, R = 8.31 J K^-1 mol^-1, T = 300 K.
(b) Uses Delta U = (3/2) nR Delta T to find Delta T = Delta U / ((3/2) nR) = 150 / (1.5 * 0.20 * 8.31) = 60.2 K.
(b) Calculates final temperature T_final = 300 + 60.2 = 360 K (accept 360 K to 360.2 K).

hints: In (a), use U = (3/2) nRT with T = 300 K.
In (b), the electrical energy supplied increases the internal energy: Delta U = 150 J. Find Delta T and add it to 300 K.
solution:
(a) Total internal energy:
U = (3/2) nRT = 1.5 * (0.20 mol) * (8.31 J K^-1 mol^-1) * (300 K) = 747.9 J = 748 J.
(b) Because the flask is rigid, no work is done on or by the gas (W = 0). By the first law of thermodynamics, Delta U = Q = 150 J.
Delta U = (3/2) nR Delta T
Delta T = Delta U / ((3/2) nR) = 150 J / (1.5 * 0.20 mol * 8.31 J K^-1 mol^-1) = 150 / 2.493 = 60.17 K.
Final temperature:
T_final = T_initial + Delta T = 300 K + 60.2 K = 360 K.
teacher_walkthrough: Part (a): Direct application of U = (3/2) nRT. 1.5 * 0.20 * 8.31 * 300 = 748 J.
Part (b): Constant volume means all heat enters internal energy: Delta U = 150 J.
Solve for Delta T: 150 / (1.5 * 0.20 * 8.31) = 60.2 K. Add to 300 K to get 360 K.
